competences: The learner explains christ as the light of the world.
The learner identifies Christian actions that demonstrate Jesus' teachings.
languageCompetence: Reads, spells and writes Jesus, Christ, light, witness, healing, forgiving, obedience and compassion.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to describe christ as the light of the world.
By the end of the lesson, learners should answer at least three authentic exercise questions about Jesus' actions and Christian witness.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already heard about Jesus' care for people and have personal experiences of helping others at home and school.
materials: P5 CRE Term III learner notes and prepared source-quotation chart
Chalkboard with lesson headings and sourced questions
references: Primary Five Religious Education past-paper collection

steps.teacherActivity: Introduce christ as the light of the world and ask learners to recall something they know about how Jesus treated people. Establish the connection to John 8:12.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners share experiences of helping people and recall prior knowledge of Jesus and his teachings.

source.quote: What John means by Jesus as the light.

steps.content: Jesus as the light of the world; Ways Jesus showed God's light. **Christ the Light** is a Christian teaching about Jesus bringing life to the world. John 8:12 describes Jesus as the light of the world. Christians believe that people who follow Jesus receive the light of life. Jesus was sent by God the Father to bring life to people.
steps.teacherActivity: Explain jesus as the light of the world and ways jesus showed god's light by writing the cited factual points. Question pupils about Jesus' words and actions while clarifying their meaning.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners copy important points, name relevant acts of Jesus, and answer short factual questions.

source.quote: What John means by Jesus as the light.

steps.content: Bible teachings about light. John 8:12 teaches that Jesus is the light of the world. Matthew 5:14–16 urges followers to shine so others see their good deeds. Christians are expected to show kindness and goodness to others. The light of Jesus is reflected when believers forgive those who wrong them.
steps.teacherActivity: Guide learners through bible teachings about light using the sourced examples. Link helpful actions to how Christians follow Jesus' teaching.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners explain the main examples of Christian witness and give corresponding facts from the lesson notes.

source.quote: WAYS IN WHICH CHRIST IS THE LIGHT OF THE WORLD

steps.content: Sourced questions: 24. State any two ways how Jesus acted like a light to us. | 12. How did Jesus make members of Lazarus’ family happy? | 13. In which way did Jesus show His love to mankind? | 5. Either: Mention any one group of people that Jesus healed during His ministry. | 32. Either : (a) Give any two ways Jesus showed love to His followers.
steps.teacherActivity: Set the five sourced questions exactly as found in the notes and past papers. Allow independent answers before discussing corrections using the cited facts.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer all five exercise questions in writing and then correct their work with guidance.

source.quote: WAYS IN WHICH CHRIST IS THE LIGHT OF THE WORLD

steps.teacherActivity: Revisit the lesson objectives and ask what learners remember about the light of Jesus. Give the source exercise questions for homework and identify remaining misconceptions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners summarise the main message and note the sourced revision task for home practice.

source.quote: WAYS IN WHICH CHRIST IS THE LIGHT OF THE WORLD

assessment: Assess the lesson using the following authentic questions: 24. State any two ways how Jesus acted like a light to us. 12. How did Jesus make members of Lazarus’ family happy? 13. In which way did Jesus show His love to mankind? 5. Either: Mention any one group of people that Jesus healed during His ministry. 32. Either : (a) Give any two ways Jesus showed love to His followers. Compare responses with the cited facts, then correct errors.
homework: Use the five sourced questions to revise what Jesus taught and how Christians show love.
